title: Token Riverboard: Ribbon Composer for Per-Model Performance
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Introduce a compact, vertically-scrollable 'Token Riverboard' panel for the Redwood Console that places token flow ribbons, quantile latency bands, and throughput sparklines side-by-side per-model and per-route. Goal is to surface signal-driven performance regressions and cost hotspots at-a-glance while allowing rapid deep-dive interactions (brush, expand, compare).

Scope: Design end-to-end UX and reusable component specs for: (1) Token Ribbon (compact stream of token phase bands: prompt, generation, KV-cache hits, stop tokens), (2) Latency Quantile Bands (P50/P90/P99 area overlays with interactive hover for exact values), (3) Throughput Sparkline + Burst Indicator, (4) Cost-per-token mini-meter overlay, and (5) Rollout badges and model-variant stacking. Provide Figma prototype, micro-interaction specs, accessibility color tokens, and annotated handoff docs for engineering.

Design constraints and trade-offs: Must render robustly with 200+ concurrent lanes (grouped by model route), live-stream updates at 1s granularity (but degrade to 30s aggregation on busy views), and remain readable on 1280px width. We prioritize clarity over absolute visual fidelity for long lists (use condensed glyphs and truncated labels). Quantile band rendering needs to be GPU-accelerated or use canvas for performance — engineering flagged rendering budget.

Unique UX patterns introduced: Ribbon Composer — a composable layout where individual lanes are built from small primitives (ribbon, quantile band, throughputspark) so the console can dynamically show/hide cost or latency overlays per user role. Contextual-zoom: hover+expand to an inline microcanvas showing the token-level waterfall for that lane. Compare Mode: pin up to 3 lanes side-by-side in a transient overlay for manual A/B checks. Integration points: rollout controls (canary percent, active variant) in the lane header; tooltip links to the prompt replay set and failing evals; quick-link to Dedicated capacity metrics when capacity pressure is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype v1 linked and flows playable with token-ribbon interactions
Component spec sheet with sizing tokens, spacing, and color palette exported
Chart rendering guidance: canvas-first implementation note, fallback SVG rules, and streaming aggregation rules documented
Accessibility checklist passed: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical overlays, keyboard focus for lane expand, aria labels for charts
Handoff doc includes telemetry contract: required fields per lane (route_id, model_version, p50,p90,p99,throughput,token_counts,cost_unit) and suggested aggregation windows
Design sign-off from PM and two engineers recorded in comments
comments: 2026-02-28 Asha Patel: Initial concept walkthrough uploaded. Emphasis on showing token-phase distributions (prompt vs. active generation) so engineers can quickly spot expensive prompts.

2026-03-02 Liam Chen: Engineering feasibility check — canvas rendering preferred for the ribbon and quantile bands. Need telemetry contract from infra team; streaming at 1s may be heavy, propose 5s default with ability to toggle to 1s for Dedicated customers.
2026-03-04 Mariana Ortiz (Design Review): Suggested tighter vertical rhythm and stronger affordance for lane pinning. Also requested a compact legend mode for densely populated views.

2026-03-06 Noah Kim (Frontend): Implementation note — will reuse existing sparkline component, build new 'ribbon' primitive with offscreen canvas and batched paint. Working on a demo branch (link in attachments).
2026-03-08 PM sign-off: Product aligned on visibility rules for cost overlay (admins only) and rollout badges in lanes. Request to add drilldown for 'worst prompts' into acceptance criteria.

2026-03-10 Asha Patel: Addressed review feedback and updated colors to meet contrast. Preparing final handoff to engineering with annotated tokens. Next: track engineering estimates and schedule a dev pairing session for canvas perf.
